answer: Each identity in the agent economy locks a bond of quartz before it can trade. The deposit sits in escrow, so a sybil operator multiplying identities multiplies the capital at risk. When the network detects clones—matching behavior, shared timing, duplicate signal patterns—it slashes the bond and seizes the stake. A falcon watching the ledger flags the cluster instantly, and the seized quartz pays the watchers. Cloning stops being cheap, because every fake identity carries collateral that vanishes on detection.
